title: Social teaching, again
tomorrow: what did Mary say when the wine ran out?

cards: Steam off a pot of tamales, the smell of corn and chile, a line out the door of the parish hall. Somewhere near the back is a man with no money, waiting anyway. So who gets served first?
The people who paid and waited, or the one who can't pay at all? The Church has a body of teaching about exactly this kind of question, and its answer has a smell of food all over it.

teach.b: Catholic social teaching is what the Church says about justice: work, wages, families, and who gets left out.
Pope Leo the Thirteenth opened a letter about workers with the Latin words Rerum Novarum, of new things, and argued that the poor, with no resources to fall back on, have a special claim to care.
The Catechism names it a preferential love for those weighed down by poverty.

teach.h: NOT THE POOR ONLY. THE POOR FIRST.
teach.b: The poor first. Not the poor only. Everyone has the same dignity.
But when there's one plate and two people, the one with nothing gets it first.
It comes straight from the Gospel. Jesus says in Matthew, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me."
Here's the one to tell a friend: Saint Ambrose tells a story about Lawrence, a deacon in Rome.
Ordered to hand over the Church's treasures, Lawrence brought out the poor, and said these were its treasures. That's the whole teaching in one scene.
The poor aren't a cost the Church carries. They're its treasure. So the tamale question has an answer: feed the man at the back first.
The line still gets fed. It just learns who comes first.

how: Catholics live out social teaching through parish food pantries, the St. Vincent de Paul Society, Catholic Charities, fair treatment of workers, and the works of mercy; the Church speaks of a preferential love for the poor.

games.q: you're running the church food table. one plate left: a regular who paid, and a man who has nothing. what does the social teaching suggest?
o: the man with nothing first, then make more for the regular.
the regular first, because he paid and waited his turn.
split the plate exactly in half between the two of them.
games.why: the Church speaks of a preferential love for the poor: first, not only. everyone still matters, and everyone still gets fed.

practice: If there's food or a drink nearby, take one slow bite or sip and really taste it; if not, remember the last good meal you had. Then bring to mind one person who will go without today.
If you pray, you can hold that person before God; if not, keep them in mind while the taste fades.
